private_notes.observations: No prior rates, allocations, or profit data are available. Our fully loaded cost is $200 per hour.
private_notes.plan: Start at a competitive rate with a meaningful margin. Use future published rates and our allocated hours to estimate how pricing affects profit, then adjust incrementally.

private_notes.observations: No prior rates or allocations are available. Fully loaded cost is $200 per hour, and both panel share and total outsourced hours may decline as rates rise.
private_notes.plan: Start at a competitive rate with a meaningful margin. Use subsequent published rates and observed allocated hours to adjust based on realized profit, rather than assuming the allocation formula.

private_notes.observations: No historical panel rates or hour allocations are available. Our fully loaded cost is $200 per hour.
private_notes.plan: Start with a competitive rate above cost, then use published panel rates and subsequent allocation outcomes to adjust for long-run profit.

private_notes.observations: In Q1, a $350 rate yielded 498 hours and approximately $74,690 profit. The other panel rates were $325 and $350. One quarter is insufficient to estimate how a rate change affects allocated hours.
private_notes.plan: Lower the rate modestly to $340 to improve competitiveness while retaining a substantial margin. Compare next quarter's hours and profit with Q1 before making a larger adjustment.

private_notes.observations: In Q1, a $325 rate against two $350 competitors yielded 821 allocated hours and approximately $102,619 profit. One quarter does not establish how sensitive hours are to price.
private_notes.plan: Raise the rate modestly toward the other panel firms' published rates while retaining a small price advantage. Compare the resulting hours and profit with Q1 before making a larger adjustment.

private_notes.observations: At $350 in Q1, we received 498 hours and earned approximately $74,690. Competitors charged $350 and $325; one observation does not establish how sensitive our allocation is to price.
private_notes.plan: Hold the Q1 rate to preserve a profitable baseline. Use subsequent rates and allocated hours to assess whether a modest change would improve long-run profit.

private_notes.observations: At $340 in Q2, Arden & Cole received 661 hours, up from 498 hours at $350 in Q1. Birchwood Hale also raised its rate from $325 to $345, so the increase in our hours cannot be attributed solely to our rate cut.
private_notes.plan: Hold at $340 to preserve the strong Q2 margin and competitive position. Use subsequent allocations and rate cards to assess whether a higher rate would improve profit without sacrificing too many hours.

private_notes.observations: At $325 in Q1, we received 821 hours and earned about $102,619. At $345 in Q2, hours fell to 598 and profit to about $86,752; Arden & Cole also lowered its rate from $350 to $340. The higher rate did not pay off, though the competitor's change contributed to the decline.
private_notes.plan: Test a lower rate to recover hours and assess whether the added volume outweighs the narrower margin. Avoid assuming the entire Q2 decline was caused by our rate change.

private_notes.observations: At $350, Calder Rowe earned about $75k in Q1 and $81k in Q2. Allocated hours rose from 498 to 541 even though both competitors priced below $350 in Q2. The allocation response to our own rate changes remains unknown.
private_notes.plan: Raise the rate modestly to $365 to test whether the additional margin outweighs any loss of hours. Compare Q3 hours and profit with the $350 baseline before making a larger change.

private_notes.observations: At $340, allocated hours fell from 661 in Q2 to 562 in Q3 as Birchwood cut its rate from $345 to $315. The Q3 allocation still produced about $78,700 in profit.
private_notes.plan: Hold $340. A small rate cut would need a meaningful increase in hours to offset the lower margin, which the limited history does not establish. Reassess after the next allocation and rate card.

private_notes.observations: Q3’s $315 rate brought 927 hours and roughly $106,600 in profit, exceeding the results at $325 in Q1 and $345 in Q2. Other firms’ rates and quarterly demand also changed, so the effect of our rate alone is uncertain.
private_notes.plan: Test a modest further reduction to see whether additional hours compensate for the lower margin. Continue optimizing our own long-run profit using observed allocations, without assuming competitors will hold their rates fixed.

private_notes.observations: At $350, quarterly profit was about $75k–$81k. Raising the rate to $365 coincided with profit falling to $56k, though Birchwood Hale also cut its rate to $315, so the effect of our increase is uncertain.
private_notes.plan: Reduce the rate to $340 to regain competitiveness while retaining a $140 hourly margin. Compare the resulting hours and profit with prior quarters before adjusting again.

private_notes.observations: At $340, allocated hours fell from 661 in Q2 to 485 in Q4 as Birchwood's rate fell from $345 to $310. Q4 profit was $67,907. A $330 rate would need about 523 hours to exceed that profit.
private_notes.plan: Reduce the rate moderately to $330 to test whether a more competitive price recovers enough hours to offset the smaller margin. Reassess using next quarter's allocation and rate card.

private_notes.observations: The Q4 reduction to $310 did not increase hours: allocation fell from 927 to 884 as Calder Rowe lowered its rate from $365 to $340. Q4 profit was $97,219, below Q3’s $106,625. Recent results suggest further rate cuts may not earn enough additional hours to offset the lower margin.
private_notes.plan: Hold at $310 for Q5 rather than chase hours with another cut. Compare the next allocation and panel rate card before making a further adjustment.

private_notes.observations: At $340 in Q4, we received 485 hours and earned about $67,900. At $350 in Q1–Q2, we earned about $74,700–$81,200; $365 in Q3 performed poorly. Competitor rates and demand varied, so these comparisons do not isolate the effect of our rate.
private_notes.plan: Return to $350 to test whether the stronger profit seen in Q1–Q2 persists. Avoid chasing the lowest panel rate; reassess after observing Q5 hours and the new rate card.

private_notes.observations: At $330 in Q5, we received 587 hours and earned $76,274. That improved on Q4's $67,907 at $340, though Calder Rowe also raised its rate, so the effect of our price change is uncertain.
private_notes.plan: Hold at $330 for another quarter to test whether the stronger allocation persists. Reassess against the next rate card and hours before changing price.

private_notes.observations: At $310, profit was about $96–97k in each of the last two quarters. The $325 rate earned about $103k in Q1; $345 earned substantially less. Competitor rates have recently been $330–$350.
private_notes.plan: Raise the rate moderately to $325 to improve margin without approaching the poorly performing $345 level. Reassess after observing the next allocation and rate card.

private_notes.observations: At $350, Q5 profit fell to about $59,000 as hours dropped to 393; the other firms charged $330 and $310. Q4's $340 rate produced about $68,000 on 485 hours. The data are noisy, but $350 looks less attractive at recent competitor rates.
private_notes.plan: Set $340 to improve competitiveness without giving up too much margin. Reassess allocated hours and the next panel rate card before considering another change.

private_notes.observations: At $330, allocated hours rose from 587 in Q5 to 631 in Q6, producing $82,006 in Q6 profit. Birchwood raised its rate from $310 to $325 while Calder lowered its rate from $350 to $340, so the increase in hours cannot be attributed to our rate alone. Prior results at $340 varied considerably with competitors' rates.

private_notes.observations: At $325 in Q6, allocated hours fell to 697 and profit to about $87,000. Rates of $310–$315 produced 875–927 hours and roughly $96,000–$107,000 in profit. The $345 rate also performed poorly.

private_notes.observations: At $340 in Q6, we received 516 hours and earned $72,306. Rival rates were $330 and $325. The prior quarter’s $350 rate produced fewer hours and $58,994 in profit, though demand and rival rates also differed.
private_notes.plan: Hold at $340. It delivered strong recent profit while remaining close to rival rates. Reassess after the next allocation and rate card rather than reacting to a single quarter.

private_notes.observations: At $330, quarterly profit has been $76,274–$82,006. Q7's lower allocation coincided with Birchwood cutting its rate from $325 to $315. Past results do not clearly show that a further rate cut would increase profit.

private_notes.observations: At $340, quarterly profit was about $72,306 in Q6 and $67,125 in Q7. The lower Q7 allocation coincided with Birchwood reducing its rate from $325 to $315. Earlier $350 quarters are less comparable because rival rates were generally higher.

private_notes.plan: Hold at $305. Avoid encouraging further panel-wide cuts; reassess if competitor rates or allocated hours change.
